Content:
Matrix exponentials can be used for solving homogeneous systems of the form
[MATH: \mathbf{x}'(t)=A\mathbf{x}(t),]
where [MATH: A] is a constant square matrix.

Content:
For example, consider the system
[MATH: {x^{′}(t) = 5y(t); y^{′}(t) = − 5x(t)]

Content:
Writing our system in matrix form, we get
[MATH: [0|5; − 5|0]]
where [MATH: [x(t); y(t)]] So, the matrix of the system is [MATH: [0|5; − 5|0]]

Content:
Recall that given the system [MATH: \mathbf{x}'(t) = A \mathbf{x}(t),] where [MATH: A] is a constant square matrix, the general solution of the system can be written as
[MATH: \mathbf{x}(t) = \Phi(t) \, \mathbf{c},]
where [MATH: \Phi(t)] is a fundamental matrix of the system, and [MATH: \mathbf{c}] is some constant vector.

Content:
Since we have already seen how to compute the standard fundamental matrix, we will not repeat the calculation here. So, computing the standard fundamental matrix [MATH: \Phi_0(t)] of the system, we get
[MATH: [\cos (5t)|\sin (5t); − \sin (5t)|\cos (5t)]]

Content:
Therefore, the general solution is

Content:
[MATH: x(t)|= Φ_{0}(t)c; = e^{At}c; = [\cos (5t)|\sin (5t); − \sin (5t)|\cos (5t)][c_{1}; c_{2}]; = c_{1}[\cos (5t); − \sin (5t)] + c_{2}[\sin (5t); \cos (5t)],]

Content:
where [MATH: c_1,c_2 \in \mathbb{R}.]

Content:
Note: Recall that for the general solution of the ordinary differential equation [MATH: x'(t)=ax(t),] we have
[MATH: x'(t)=ax(t)
\qquad\Rightarrow\qquad
x(t) = c \, e^{at},
\quad
c \in \mathbb{R}.]
Now, for the general solution of the matrix differential equation [MATH: \mathbf{x}'(t)=A\mathbf{x}(t),] we obtain
[MATH: \mathbf{x}'(t)=A\mathbf{x}(t)
\qquad\Rightarrow\qquad
\mathbf{x}(t) = e^{At} \, \mathbf{c},
\quad
\mathbf{c} \in \mathbb{R}^n.]

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Matrix exponentials can be used for solving homogeneous systems of the form
[MATH: \mathbf{x}'(t)=A\mathbf{x}(t),]
where [MATH: A] is a constant square matrix.

Content:
For example, consider the system
[MATH: {x^{′}(t) = 5y(t); y^{′}(t) = − 5x(t)]

Content:
Writing our system in matrix form, we get
[MATH: [0|5; − 5|0]]
where [MATH: [x(t); y(t)]] So, the matrix of the system is [MATH: [0|5; − 5|0]]

Content:
Recall that given the system [MATH: \mathbf{x}'(t) = A \mathbf{x}(t),] where [MATH: A] is a constant square matrix, the general solution of the system can be written as
[MATH: \mathbf{x}(t) = \Phi(t) \, \mathbf{c},]
where [MATH: \Phi(t)] is a fundamental matrix of the system, and [MATH: \mathbf{c}] is some constant vector.

Content:
Since we have already seen how to compute the standard fundamental matrix, we will not repeat the calculation here. So, computing the standard fundamental matrix [MATH: \Phi_0(t)] of the system, we get
[MATH: [\cos (5t)|\sin (5t); − \sin (5t)|\cos (5t)]]

Content:
Therefore, the general solution is

Content:
[MATH: x(t)|= Φ_{0}(t)c; = e^{At}c; = [\cos (5t)|\sin (5t); − \sin (5t)|\cos (5t)][c_{1}; c_{2}]; = c_{1}[\cos (5t); − \sin (5t)] + c_{2}[\sin (5t); \cos (5t)],]

Content:
where [MATH: c_1,c_2 \in \mathbb{R}.]

Content:
Note: Recall that for the general solution of the ordinary differential equation [MATH: x'(t)=ax(t),] we have
[MATH: x'(t)=ax(t)
\qquad\Rightarrow\qquad
x(t) = c \, e^{at},
\quad
c \in \mathbb{R}.]
Now, for the general solution of the matrix differential equation [MATH: \mathbf{x}'(t)=A\mathbf{x}(t),] we obtain
[MATH: \mathbf{x}'(t)=A\mathbf{x}(t)
\qquad\Rightarrow\qquad
\mathbf{x}(t) = e^{At} \, \mathbf{c},
\quad
\mathbf{c} \in \mathbb{R}^n.]

Content:
Let's see more examples.

---

Item 2 — Example: Finding the General Solution of a Homogeneous System Using a Given Matrix Exponential

Example Prompt:
[MATH: {x^{′}(t) = − 7x(t) + y(t); y^{′}(t) = − 7y(t)]
Find the general solution to the system of ODEs above.

Hint: [MATH: [e^{− 7t}|te^{− 7t}; 0|e^{− 7t}]] where [MATH: [− 7|1; 0|− 7]]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Writing our system in matrix form, we get
[MATH: [− 7|1; 0|− 7]]
where [MATH: [x(t); y(t)]] So, the matrix of the system is [MATH: [− 7|1; 0|− 7]]

Given the system [MATH: \mathbf{x}'(t) = A \mathbf{x}(t),] where [MATH: A] is a constant square matrix, the general solution of the system can be written as
[MATH: \mathbf{x}(t) = \Phi(t) \, \mathbf{c},]
where [MATH: \Phi(t)] is a fundamental matrix of the system, and [MATH: \mathbf{c}] is a constant vector.

Now, using the given information, the standard fundamental matrix [MATH: \Phi_0(t)] of the system is given by
[MATH: [e^{− 7t}|te^{− 7t}; 0|e^{− 7t}]]

Therefore, the general solution is

[MATH: x(t)|= Φ_{0}(t)c; = e^{At}c; = [e^{− 7t}|te^{− 7t}; 0|e^{− 7t}][c_{1}; c_{2}]; = c_{1}[e^{− 7t}; 0] + c_{2}[te^{− 7t}; e^{− 7t}]; = c_{1}[1; 0]e^{− 7t} + c_{2}[t; 1]e^{− 7t},]

where [MATH: c_1,c_2 \in \mathbb{R}.]

Item 5 — Tutorial: Solving Initial Value Problems

Content:
Now, let's find the solution to the initial value problem below
[MATH: {x^{′}(t) = 7x(t) + y(t); y^{′}(t) = 7y(t),]

Content:

[MATH: [7|1; 0|7]]
where [MATH: [x(t); y(t)]] So, the matrix of the system is [MATH: [7|1; 0|7]]

Content:
Recall that the general solution of the system [MATH: \mathbf{x}'(t) = A \mathbf{x}(t),] where [MATH: A] is a constant square matrix, can be written as
[MATH: \mathbf{x}(t) = \Phi_0(t) \, \mathbf{c},]
where [MATH: \Phi_0(t) = e^{At}] is the standard fundamental matrix of the system, and [MATH: \mathbf{c}] is some constant vector.

Content:
Evaluating both sides of [MATH: \mathbf{x}(t) = e^{At} \mathbf{c}] at [MATH: t=0,] we get
[MATH: x(0)|= Φ_{0}(0)c; x(0)|= e^{A(0)}c; x(0)|= Ic; c|= x(0).]

Content:
Thus, the solution to our initial value problem is
[MATH: \mathbf{x}(t) = \Phi_0(t) \, \mathbf{x}(0).]

Content:
Computing the standard fundamental matrix [MATH: \Phi_0(t)] of the system, we get

Content:
Therefore, the solution is

Content:
[MATH: x(t)|= e^{At}x(0); = [e^{7t}|te^{7t}; 0|e^{7t}][3; − 2]; = [(3 − 2t)e^{7t}; − 2e^{7t}].]
